name: Eswatini
summary: A kingdom you can cross in two hours, with rhino at Hlane and Mkhaya, granite whalebacks at Sibebe and Execution Rock, and the Umhlanga and Incwala ceremonies that are the living centre of the country's year.
when: May to September — dry, cooler and best for game. Umhlanga is in late August or early September.

entries.caption: Small, and Full
entries.description: Two hours across, and it holds rhino, rainforest gorges, granite domes and a living monarchy.
entries.subject: the Ezulwini valley with granite hills on both sides

entries.caption: Highveld to Lowveld
entries.description: Fourteen hundred metres in the west down to two hundred in the east, in sixty kilometres.
entries.subject: the escarpment dropping from highveld to lowveld

entries.caption: Rhino at Mkhaya
entries.description: Black and white rhino, tracked on foot, in a private reserve that has never lost one to poaching.
entries.subject: a black rhino among thorn scrub at Mkhaya

entries.caption: Hlane and Mkhaya
entries.description: Lion and elephant at Hlane, rhino and sable at Mkhaya, both small and both excellent.
entries.subject: lions resting under a tree in Hlane Royal National Park

entries.caption: Sibebe
entries.description: The largest exposed granite dome in the world after Uluru, and you walk up it.
entries.subject: the bare granite dome of Sibebe rock above the valley

entries.caption: Mantenga
entries.description: A wide falls beside the cultural village in the Ezulwini valley.
entries.subject: the Mantenga falls spreading over rock in the Ezulwini valley

entries.caption: The Great Usutu
entries.description: The country's main river, running east through a gorge to the Mozambican border.
entries.subject: the Great Usutu river running through a rocky gorge

entries.caption: Landlocked, and Close
entries.description: No coast — but the Mozambican beaches at Ponta do Ouro are two hours from Manzini.
entries.subject: a river pool with rocks and trees in the Malolotja valley

entries.caption: Malolotja and Ngwempisi
entries.description: Montane grassland and Afromontane forest in the northwest, with proper wilderness walking.
entries.subject: montane grassland and forest patches at Malolotja

entries.caption: Canopy Tours and Whitewater
entries.description: The Malolotja canopy tour, and rafting the Great Usutu when it is up.
entries.subject: a canopy tour zipline crossing a forested gorge at Malolotja

entries.caption: A Living Monarchy
entries.description: Umhlanga and Incwala are not performances — they are the constitutional year.
entries.subject: young women in ceremonial dress at the Umhlanga reed dance

entries.caption: The Swazi
entries.description: One nation, one language, and a set of ceremonies that everyone in the country takes part in.
entries.subject: Swazi men in traditional dress at a royal ceremony

entries.caption: Sidvudvu and Emasi
entries.description: Pumpkin with maize, emasi soured milk, and braai everywhere.
entries.subject: a bowl of sidvudvu pumpkin porridge

entries.caption: Umhlanga and Incwala
entries.description: The reed dance in late August, and Incwala, the kingship ceremony, in December and January.
entries.subject: the reed dance procession at Umhlanga

entries.caption: Candles, Glass and Weaving
entries.description: Swazi Candles, Ngwenya Glass from recycled bottles, and Gone Rural's grass weaving.
entries.subject: hand-made Swazi candles in bright patterns on a bench

entries.caption: Ngwenya Mine
entries.description: Iron ore mined here forty-three thousand years ago — among the oldest mines on earth.
entries.subject: the red iron ore workings of the ancient Ngwenya mine

entries.caption: Nothing Listed, Everything Living
entries.description: No World Heritage sites, and a ceremonial calendar that has never been interrupted.
entries.subject: a Swazi homestead of beehive huts within a reed fence

entries.caption: Mbabane and Manzini
entries.description: A small capital in the hills, and the commercial town and market in the middle.
entries.subject: the market and streets of Manzini

entries.caption: Beehive and Colonial
entries.description: Woven beehive huts in the homesteads, and small colonial towns in stone.
entries.subject: a woven grass beehive hut at a Swazi homestead

entries.caption: The Manzini Market
entries.description: Produce downstairs, handicraft upstairs, and the whole country passing through on a Thursday.
entries.subject: the handicraft section of Manzini market

entries.caption: Easy and Safe
entries.description: Short distances, malaria-light, rhino you can walk to, and a very gentle pace.
entries.subject: a family on a guided walk towards rhino at Mkhaya

entries.caption: Walking Malolotja
entries.description: Multi-day wilderness trails across grassland and gorge, with huts and no roads.
entries.subject: a walking trail crossing open grassland at Malolotja

entries.caption: Small and Good
entries.description: Mkhaya's Stone Camp, and lodges through the Ezulwini valley.
entries.subject: an open-sided stone and thatch camp in the bush at Mkhaya

entries.caption: Big Game Parks
entries.description: One family has run Hlane, Mkhaya and Mlilwane since 1960, and brought the rhino back.
entries.subject: a ranger tracking rhino on foot at Mkhaya

entries.caption: Granite and Grass
entries.description: Sibebe in the late afternoon, when the whole dome goes orange.
entries.subject: late sun on the granite dome of Sibebe

entries.caption: Ngwempisi Gorge
entries.description: A wilderness gorge in the west with hanging bridges and no vehicles.
entries.subject: a suspension bridge over the forested Ngwempisi gorge

entries.caption: Why Eswatini
entries.description: Rhino on foot, a monarchy in ceremony, and a country you can cross before lunch.
entries.subject: a rhino at close range from a walking trail at Mkhaya
